_note: Sixteen curated generation seeds. RE-CURATED 2026-11-05 (Ben, BL-1413: all sixteen) off a 96-seed exploration_sweep pool (seeds 0..95) at main f5cd40c9: seeds 0, 46, 31 and 13 kept, twelve replaced, each `replaces` naming the seed whose purpose it took. First chosen 2026-09-16 off a 48-seed parity sweep; four replaced 2026-09-17 (NR-887).

A SEED IS THE SAVE. Generation is a pure function of the world descriptor, so a seed reproduces its world exactly on a given binary; there is no separate snapshot format and none is needed. What a seed cannot carry is why it was chosen, which is what this store holds.

THE FINGERPRINT IS NOT A GOLDEN. It is five counters from seed_library_sweep.json at the repo root, and a world-moving item is SUPPOSED to move them. Re-read with `node tools/session/seed_library.js --check` after such an item, and `--bless` once the movement is authorised. The rationale is the part that survives; the numbers are there so a future session can tell whether the world it generates is still the world described.
THE POOL WAS SWEPT AT PARITY (BL-1007): scripts/world_gen.lua and scripts/works.lua, the shipped data layer. Readings taken before 2026-09-16 describe a different world and do not compare.

To check or bless, regenerate the library's own table first: `build_gen/verify/exploration_sweep.exe --seeds $(node tools/session/seed_library.js --seed-list) --out seed_library_sweep.json` (BL-1026). The checked-in exploration_sweep.json carries seeds 0..15 only and is not the library's table.

A `review` field marks a seed whose rationale is under Ben's review in NEEDS_REVIEW, naming the entry and the candidates; it is removed when he rules. A `replaces` field records which seed an entry took the place of, and why.

READINGS AND RATIONALE REWRITTEN 2026-10-07 (Ben's ruling, after the sprint 49 re-bless) from seed_library_sweep.json at main c77f2d5a, with haulage from docs/development/drafts/sprint-49-rebless.md. The lake cap (BL-1200) redrew every world. Rankings in the `why` lines are against the other fifteen library seeds, not the 48-seed curation pool, which has not been re-swept.

CAPITAL IS NEARLY FLAT ON THIS BINARY (2026-11-05): 82 of the 96 pool seeds hold a median polity chest within 10% of 69M. The treasury purposes are served by the outliers (seeds 7 and 46 high, 29 low) and the other purposes aim at the axes that vary - polities 23-187, post roads 17-222, subjects 0-10, neighbour wars 0-328. Rankings in the `why` lines are against the other fifteen library seeds unless they name the pool.

seeds.name: The reference world
seeds.why: Seed 0 is the descriptor default and the world every harness, capture and golden is written about. It belongs here because a library needs the world everything else is compared against, not because it is unusual. On this binary it sits in the upper middle on most axes: 83 polities, 78 flows, 164 post roads, 18,991 Empire battles, displacement 79.8.

seeds.name: The rich world
seeds.why: The second-richest world in the library, with a median polity chest of 130.8M against a library-typical 69M (only seed 7 is higher), and a 1.25B top chest. It is also busy: 13,399 flow volume (third) and 145 post roads. Its Exploration conflict is all frontier, 669 battles against no neighbour war. If chartering cannot form here it cannot form anywhere, so it is the ceiling case.

seeds.name: The wealth that stayed home
seeds.why: The richest world in the pool, at a 171.9M median polity chest, and the one that fought least in Exploration: seven battles, all frontier, too few to read a displacement verdict (SILENT). Twenty-six polities, the fewest in the library, hold ten subjects, tied for the most. Capital that never left home: the case for an Industrialisation that inherits money and no outward habit.

replaces.why: 38's wealth-at-home case had reversed (its chest fell to the library middle and its conflict turned outward); 7 has the highest median chest in the 96-seed pool and almost no Exploration fighting

seeds.name: The inward world
seeds.why: The inward extreme: 230 neighbour wars against 10 frontier battles, displacement 0.04, HELD. It has the lowest flow volume in the library (2,352), the fewest standing treaties (15) and 33 polities. Whatever the phase does here, it does with almost no outward turn.

replaces.why: no library seed read HELD once seed 12 turned outward (displacement 26.1); 3 is the pool's most inward world

seeds.name: The no-neighbour frontier
seeds.why: Displaced with no neighbour war at all: 2,334 frontier battles, the most in the library, against zero, so the ratio is undefined and the verdict reads displaced(no-nb). It also has the lowest median polity chest in the library, 57.2M, so it doubles as the poor case on a binary where capital barely varies.

replaces.why: 9 had stopped reading displaced(no-nb) - it had twelve neighbour wars; 29 reads it with the most frontier battles in the library

seeds.name: The colonial world
seeds.why: Twelve subjections formed, the most in the library, and ten subjects alive at 1660, tied with seed 7 for the most: a colonial age that held. Fifty-two polities, 41 post roads and 37 flows. The preferred-seller ties Exploration hands forward are densest here.

replaces.why: 41's colonial ties without capital had reversed (three subjects and a high chest); 92 formed the most subjections in the library and kept ten

seeds.name: The concentrated small world
seeds.why: A thin political map holding a deep top chest: 37 polities and a 1.27B top chest, eighteen times the 71.8M median. Displacement 287 (574 frontier battles against two neighbour wars). The case for a world where one or two polities own most of the money.

replaces.why: 43's concentrated wealth in a thin map had gone; 2 has 37 polities and a top chest eighteen times its median

seeds.name: The road world
seeds.why: 171 post roads, the second most in the library after seed 60, on middling trade (63 flows, 9,779 volume): 17.5 roads per thousand units moved, the highest outside the library's busiest worlds. Infrastructure ahead of traffic. Displacement 135.7.

replaces.why: 32's roads without traffic had gone (its roads fell to the library middle and its haulage rose); 54 lays the most roads per unit of trade outside the busiest worlds

seeds.name: The quiet world
seeds.why: The floor of the political map: 496 corridors and 19 flows, both the fewest in the library, with 35 polities, 19 post roads and 2,567 Empire battles. Its Exploration conflict is all frontier (174 battles, no neighbour war). Industrialisation has to produce something legible from a thin network here.

replaces.why: re-curated 2026-11-05 (Ben: all sixteen); 17 now holds the floor on corridors and flows

seeds.name: The crowded world
seeds.why: The most crowded world in the pool by far: 187 living polities against a next-best of 125, on only 41 flows and 8,466 Empire battles. Many small polities with thin trade between them, and the largest top chest in the library (2.18B). The hardest case for anything run per polity per round.

replaces.why: re-curated 2026-11-05 (Ben: all sixteen); 27 has 187 polities, the most in the 96-seed pool by a wide margin

seeds.name: The trade-dense world
seeds.why: The busiest network in the library: 106 flows, the most, on 17,430 volume and 3,372 corridors (both second), with 365 standing treaties. Displacement 588. The best world to watch prices form on, because there is already something moving.

seeds.name: The neighbour-war world
seeds.why: 328 neighbour wars, the most in the pool, against 123 frontier battles: displacement 0.38, HELD. Fifty-three polities and 40 flows. Conflict that stayed between neighbours: the second held world beside seed 3, and the busier of the two.

replaces.why: re-curated 2026-11-05 (Ben: all sixteen); 12 had turned outward (displacement 26.1); 22 has the most neighbour wars in the pool

seeds.name: The frontier world
seeds.why: The most displaced world in the library: 1,014 frontier battles against one neighbour war, displacement 1,014. Two subjections formed and one subject alive, the fewest: the conflict moved outward and almost nobody was subjected. A test that trade relationships form without an overlord graph to inherit.

seeds.name: The colonial-undone world
seeds.why: Ten subjections formed and four freed, the most freed in the library, with six subjects alive: a colonial age that partly came undone. It also moves the most goods of the sixteen, 19,390 volume on 90 flows. The case for ties that broke inside a busy economy.

replaces.why: re-curated 2026-11-05 (Ben: all sixteen); 64 freed the most subjects in the library

seeds.name: The roadless traders
seeds.why: Seventeen post roads, the fewest in the library, carrying 26 flows: the most trade per road of the sixteen. Thirty polities and 1,801 Empire battles (the fewest), all of its Exploration fighting frontier. Trade that barely bought a road.

replaces.why: re-curated 2026-11-05 (Ben: all sixteen); 37 now has 125 post roads; 63 has the fewest in the library

seeds.name: The big busy world
seeds.why: Large, violent and commercial at once: 22,161 Empire battles, 2,516 Exploration battles, 200 post roads, 3,663 corridors and 418 standing treaties, the most of the sixteen on all five, with 125 polities and 79 flows. Neighbour and frontier war both run hot (239 against 2,277). The stress case for whatever Industrialisation runs per polity per round.

replaces.why: re-curated 2026-11-05 (Ben: all sixteen); 60 leads the library on Empire and Exploration battles, roads, corridors and treaties
